tagline: Philips' hometown has become the Netherlands' capital of design and technology, with Dutch Design Week, the GLOW light festival and PSV football.
overview: Eindhoven was a small town until 1891, when Philips began making light bulbs here; the company's factories turned it into the Netherlands' fifth-largest city. The Philips Museum is in the original light-bulb factory, and Strijp-S, a former Philips industrial site, is now a creative district of lofts, studios and food halls.

Today the region, known as Brainport, is one of Europe's leading technology hubs, home to the chip machine maker ASML and the Eindhoven University of Technology. The Design Academy Eindhoven and the yearly Dutch Design Week make it the country's design capital.

In November the GLOW festival fills the streets with light art, a nod to the city's light-bulb roots. PSV Eindhoven, founded by Philips, is one of the country's biggest football clubs, and the Van Abbemuseum has a strong modern art collection.
